findings.where: Screen 2 (More fuel, wider angle), its demonstration
findings.what: The words are about more fuel pushing the rotor ahead, but the demo ramps the load from 0 to 600 kW: the Load label climbs, both bars grow and the frequency falls 62.40 to 60.97 Hz, and the words mention none of it. Either ramp A's setting at a fixed 600 kW so δ and A's kW grow from fuel alone, or add one sentence that the load is coming on and each governor adds fuel as the board slows.

findings.where: Screen 9 (Two flat lines), the Why and the say line after Check
findings.what: "It draws 50.4 kW as a motor" and "A carries 450.4 kW" are stated as fact, but the 10% motoring draw is an example value, labelled only in the hidden description; say on screen that 50.4 kW is an example figure.

findings.where: Lesson scope, against the brief's decision "Generator neutrals get one SHOW screen in lesson 6"
findings.what: There is no neutral screen at all: nothing on third harmonics adding in the neutral between paralleled sets, 2/3 pitch, earthing only one neutral, or coupled boards coupling their insulation monitors. The i7 and i8 plans do not take it, so it is lost unless it is added here.

findings.where: The interactive's Droop control, and the brief's house-diagram plan ("Tilt one line flatter and the shares drift apart as load changes")
findings.what: Both sets share one Droop slider, so the lesson never shows what unequal droops do. That leaves the operator's rule that every set needs the same droop untaught, and lesson 4 did not teach it either. Let one set's droop be dragged, and add a screen where the load is stepped and the shares drift apart.

findings.where: Screen 8 (Less droop), the first instruction and its read
findings.what: "Turn both droops down to 1%" asks him to do what the screen has already done: it opens at 1%. Both settings have also moved from 62.4 to 60.6 Hz without a word. The read replacement, "With both droops at 1%.", is a sentence fragment. Say instead that both droops are now 1%, set to 60.6 Hz so that full load still gives 60 Hz.
"To move load but hold the frequency, raise one setting and lower the other by the same amount" is a second idea, and this screen does not show it; leave it to screen 14 and the practice section.

findings.where: Screen 11 (More field on A), the question
findings.what: "What moves most?" weighs volts against kVAr against kW; ask "What happens?" as screens 5 and 9 do.
The right answer is the second choice in all three, and the final check enforces it; vary the position so the pattern cannot be learned.

findings.where: Screen 12 (Cross current), "That extra 30 kVAr flows out of A and into B"
findings.what: B's tile still shows 195 kVAr going out, so "into B" can puzzle him. Add one sentence: each set carries its fair 225 kVAr, plus or minus a 30 kVAr part that runs round between the sets instead of to the load.

It repeats lesson 4's analogy almost word for word (two cells in parallel, with internal resistance as the droop). Choose a fresh one, or keep it short and use it only for the new part, the cross current between two strings at different voltages.
The term is defined, highlighted, and never used again. The brief wanted it as the stiff board on which fuel moves only kW. Either use it once, for example for a set on shore supply, or drop it.

findings.where: Explain, paragraph 2, "the in-step part of the current"
findings.what: "In step" already means the rotor locked to the board, and here it means in phase with V. Say "the part of the current in phase with V" so the one phrase does not carry two meanings.
[^4] appears twice, and [^5] sits on a sentence about set points that he would never look up; trim the footnotes to three or four, on the rules themselves.

findings.where: Screens 4 to 7 and 14, the board at 60.97 to 61.17 Hz
findings.what: Every kW screen runs the board about 1 Hz above its rated 60 Hz, and no screen remarks on it, though the practice section does. One sentence on screen 4 would stop the question: moving both settings down together brings it back to 60 Hz.

findings.where: House diagram, the share bars' A and B labels
findings.what: Both labels sit at x = 8, under the axis, a quarter of the width away from bars that start at the load's edges, and B's bar grows from the right; put each label at its own bar's edge.

findings.where: Screen 10 (Voltage and kVAr), the example voltage droop
findings.what: 1 V per 30 kVAr is 21 V, or 4.8%, at 630 kVAr, which is close to a typical factory droop of 5% at full load and zero power factor. One sentence saying so would make the example feel less arbitrary.

findings.where: Lesson scope, against the brief's lesson 6 row
findings.what: Three of the brief's items are left out. The droop CT's shorting switch on a set running alone is missing, and so is the misconception the brief lists, "thinking the droop CT matters on a single running set". The commissioning order is missing: match the no-load voltages, trim speed to zero kW exchange, then trim voltage to cancel the circulating current. The one line on running against the mains is missing too.

findings.where: Screen 1, the opening state at 360 px
findings.what: The lesson opens on a bare recall question with no picture. The house diagram first appears on screen 2, so the opening view does not show the thing he will move.
